dedupe_keys.name: adaptive restoration of the former salin de giraud saltworks camargue

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the restoration since 2011 of 6,500 hectares of former saltworks at Salin-de-Giraud in the Rhône delta, France, used for salt production from 1950 to 2008 and then bought by the Conservatoire du Littoral. About 70 percent of the Camargue lies below 1 m, and a 100-year storm surge under a high-end scenario could reach 1.6 to 1.8 m by 2100; BRGM submersion models built on LIDAR guided the strategy. The Camargue Regional Natural Park, Tour du Valat and the National Society for Nature Protection stopped seawater pumping, dredged channels, reconnected former ponds with lagoons, the river and the sea, and abandoned seafront dykes so a natural shoreline can form, while the inland dyke of 1859 is adapted to protect the delta. Reconnection works cost under 1.5 million euros, and maintaining the 16 km inner dyke system is estimated at 7 to 13 million euros plus 80,000 to 140,000 euros a year, less than keeping the seafront dykes. The page, published in 2019 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to Tour du Valat and the Conservatoire du Littoral. Caveats: residents resisted abandoning the sea dyke, and wetland response to sea level rise remains uncertain. It illustrates nature-based coastal flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation of coastal defences; related records are the Titchwell Marsh and Hedwige and Prosper polders case studies.
name: Adaptive restoration of the former Salin-de-Giraud saltworks (Camargue)
organisations: Société nationale de protection de la nature
outcomes: Restored lagoons and marshes show saltmarsh succession, healthy benthic communities and better connectivity, and the site buffers storms at lower cost than holding the seafront dykes.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Tour du Valat research institute
resources_used: BRGM marine submersion models using LIDAR
environmental monitoring of hydrology and ecology
